stem: Two screws both measure between 2 cm and 3 cm on a ruler marked only in whole centimetres. What is the best way to find which screw is longer?
options: Measure both screws again with the same whole-centimetre ruler
Use a ruler whose each centimetre is divided into 10 equal parts
Round both lengths up to 3 cm and compare the rounded values
Measure both screws in metres, which is a bigger unit
explanation: Correct option: (B). When two lengths fall between the same two whole-number marks, splitting the unit into smaller equal parts (tenths of a cm) shows the difference. Measuring again with the same ruler gives no new information, rounding hides the difference, and a bigger unit like the metre makes it even harder to see.

stem: Shylaja's hand is 12 4/10 units long and her palm is 6 7/10 units long. What is the length of her middle finger (hand minus palm)?
explanation: Correct option: (D). We cannot take 7 tenths from 4 tenths, so split 1 unit from 12: 12 4/10 = 11 14/10. stem: The sequence 5 7/10, 5 3/10, 4 9/10, ... decreases by the same amount each time. What is its sixth term?
explanation: Correct option: (B). Each term is 4/10 less than the one before. Terms: 5 7/10, 5 3/10, 4 9/10, 4 5/10, 4 1/10, 3 7/10. From 4 1/10, take 4/10 by regrouping: 4 1/10 = 3 11/10, and 11/10 - 4/10 = 7/10, so the sixth term is 3 7/10. 4 1/10 is the fifth term, 3 3/10 is one step too far, and 4 3/10 comes from subtracting 1/10 - 4/10 as 4/10 - 1/10 without regrouping.

stem: In the decimal system, why is a unit split into 10 equal parts rather than some other number?
options: Each place value is 10 times the place value to its right
A unit can be split only into 10 equal parts and no other number
Rulers are always made exactly 10 centimetres long
Ten small parts are easier to draw than four or five parts
explanation: Correct option: (A). In the Indian place value system, each place is 10 times the one on its right (and one-tenth of the one on its left). Splitting a unit into 10 parts continues this pattern to tenths, hundredths and so on. A unit can be split into 4 or 16 parts too, so that option is false; ruler length and ease of drawing are not the reason.

stem: Which is the correct way to read 0.274, and why?
options: Zero point two hundred seventy-four, since 274 is a three-digit number
Two hundred seventy-four, since the zero before the point can be ignored
Zero point twenty-seven four, since the first two digits form tenths
Zero point two seven four, since it is 2 tenths, 7 hundredths and 4 thousandths
explanation: Correct option: (D). After the decimal point each digit has its own place value: 2 tenths, 7 hundredths, 4 thousandths, so the digits are read one by one. 1.009, because 9 thousandths is more than 0 thousandths

stem: A girl measures an opening as 2 ft 5 inches but asks the carpenter for a door 2.5 ft wide. Why does the door not fit? (1 ft = 12 inches)
options: 0.5 ft is 5 inches, so the door is exactly the right width
0.5 ft is 6 inches, so the door is 1 inch too wide
0.5 ft is 50 inches, so the door is far too wide
2.5 ft is 25 inches, so the door is far too narrow
explanation: Correct option: (B). Feet are split into 12 inches, not 10 parts, so 0.5 ft = 12 / 2 = 6 inches and 2.5 ft = 2 ft 6 inches, which is 1 inch wider than the 2 ft 5 inch opening. Reading 0.5 ft as 5 inches is the girl's mistake; 50 inches and 25 inches come from ignoring the units altogether.
